stem: A nonpregnant adult has a 2-hour plasma glucose of 165 mg/dL during a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test. How should the nurse interpret this result using ADA 2026 criteria?

options.A: It is within the ADA 2-hour plasma glucose range below impaired glucose tolerance.
options.B: It meets the ADA 2-hour plasma glucose criterion for diabetes.
options.C: It meets the ADA range for impaired glucose tolerance used to define prediabetes.
options.D: It cannot be interpreted because a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test is not used to assess prediabetes or diabetes.

rationale: ADA 2026 defines impaired glucose tolerance as a 2-hour plasma glucose of 140-199 mg/dL during a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test. A value of 165 mg/dL falls in that range. The diabetes threshold is 2-hour plasma glucose at least 200 mg/dL during the same standardized test. Therefore C is correct; A, B, and D conflict with the cited criteria.
educational_objective: Interpret a standardized 2-hour 75-g oral glucose tolerance test using current ADA criteria for impaired glucose tolerance and diabetes.
source_document_title: 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
source_version_date: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Diabetes Care 49(Suppl. 1)
source_locator: Table 2.2 and Prediabetes section: 2-h PG during 75-g OGTT 140-199 mg/dL defines impaired glucose tolerance/prediabetes; Table 2.1: 2-h PG >=200 mg/dL during 75-g OGTT is a diabetes criterion
source_claim_supported: In nonpregnant individuals, a 2-hour plasma glucose of 140-199 mg/dL during a standardized 75-g OGTT defines impaired glucose tolerance/prediabetes; >=200 mg/dL is a diabetes diagnostic threshold.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential, printed p.13/PDF p.17: Perform diagnostic testing; Monitor results of diagnostic and laboratory tests

correction_summary: Replaced the nonstandard '2-hour postprandial after a big meal' scenario with an explicitly standardized 75-g OGTT, added a concrete 165 mg/dL value, and applied the exact ADA 2026 IGT and diabetes thresholds. This removes the invalid assumption that ordinary post-meal glucose can be interpreted using OGTT diagnostic cut points.
